digest.component_or_area: LLM review gate, cost/quality metrics, Bedrock provider integration, observability
propositions: Plan-review costs $3.02/run, code-review $1.42/run, completion-verifier $2.24/run, with mean per-ticket cost $11.85 across the Bedrock gate fleet.

Cheap-model experiments (Nova Pro, Haiku) rejected for agentic review (Nova blocking-criteria recall 50-57%) but identified bounded Nova pilots and terminal-failure fixes as credible next cost levers.

Code-review's ordinal severity axes are structurally inert (0.13% LLM contribution to blocking decisions) because blocking is criterion-routed with 98.2% of LLM findings assigned to non-blocking-enabled routes, and the 0.95 impact threshold is unreachable (no real findings exceed p99=0.60).

Observability.sh probe defects fabricate false-positive metric emissions via absent offset cold-start seeding (widespread-zealous-narwhal) and substring grep over review-bot LLM prose (colossal-slothful-grouse), triggering alarms on non-events.

Deprecation survey found zero scheduled removals met their conditions; Tier 1 candidate (gitattributes migration arm) is genuinely dead; Tier 2 candidates (single-pass review surfaces, REBAR_LLM_MODEL) are 8-11 days old in the current release and need operator decision for a pre-1.0 breaking window.

Ordinal-to-binary migration plan (Phases 0-3) is complete and durable but execution remains separate work requiring operator approval; Phase 3 for code-review is blocked pending threshold/aggregation fix decision per the recovered 3,230-finding verification corpus.
